NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>The source shows a street-facing brick volume with a stepped left edge, a narrow four-part window stack, two recessed glazed balcony bays, seven dark vertical cladding bays, an upper glazed pavilion, thin roof edges, and a recessed ground-floor entrance behind brick boundary walls. CURRENT preserves these principal landmarks and their broad proportions. The strongest discrepancies are the ground-floor right enclosure and brick coursing. Rear elevations, roof depths and concealed connections are not established by the single source photograph; screenshots alone cannot verify concealed joints.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: Beneath the right brick volume, SOURCE shows a dark recessed glazed frontage. CURRENT instead exposes broad orange wall faces and a prominent brick-colored support beside the entrance, changing the visible ground-floor enclosure.
action: Locally revise this bay to reproduce the source-visible dark recessed glazing and slim framing; retain the entrance position and continuous fascia above.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: CURRENT brick courses are substantially taller and more uniformly flat than SOURCE’s fine, closely spaced horizontal brickwork. This affects both the main facade and boundary walls.
action: Reduce brick course height and adjust the brick material toward the source’s muted reddish-brown variation and fine mortar relief, preserving existing facade outlines and openings.</issue>
<keep>Seven vertical bays of dark cladding with the intermediate horizontal joint.
Two stacked balconies, with the lower balcony wider than the upper.
Three-column upper pavilion glazing and its thin projecting dark roof edge.
Four vertically stacked glazed sections in the narrow right-hand opening.</keep>
